question.text: Which document should a retirement adviser recommend a client prepare to avoid disputes over asset distribution after death?

answer.text: Only nominations in all financial accounts
A comprehensive and registered Will along with aligned nominations
An informal letter to family members about asset wishes
A verbal communication to the eldest family member

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p213-214 and p219-220, estate planning should document wishes through a legal Will; nominations simplify payment of proceeds, and heirs under the Will take precedence over nominees. A written Will supported by aligned nominations reduces conflict among heirs. The Trap: Nominations alone (Option A) do not determine ownership — they only facilitate transfer. Informal letters (Option C) and verbal communication (Option D) have no legal standing. Note: Per the workbook, registering the Will is good practice but not compulsory; the source does not state that registration provides the strongest legal standing.
